name: Password reset requests not rate limited
description:
The password-reset request can be repeated for one account without limit: a run of reset requests for the declared test identity was each answered normally and each delivered its own message to the test inbox, with no sign of throttling (no HTTP 429 or 503, no Retry-After or rate-limit header, no "too many requests" wording).

An attacker can flood any user's inbox with reset messages, and when reset tokens are guessable every extra request is one more live token to guess.

burpsy reports this only when every request it sent delivered a message: an application that throttles silently, answering alike but sending nothing, is not reported. A limit above the number of requests sent is not ruled out; the finding states that number.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's issue catalogue has no password-reset rows.
remediation: Limit reset requests per account and per client (for example a few per hour). Answer the excess without sending mail, with the same response as a normal request so the limit does not reveal which accounts exist.

references.title: OWASP WSTG: Testing for Weak Password Change or Reset Functionalities (WSTG-ATHN-09)
